anchor: Measured decile dispersion of gross pay for full-time employees, per country: how far the bottom ten percent and the top ten percent sit from that country's own median. Feeds wage_p10_usd and wage_p90_usd in data/economic_indicators/country_profile_v2.json via scripts/data/apply_wage_deciles.ts, which the country page renders as the spread on its customers card (notation N9, 2026-08-30).

convention.unit: ratio to the same source's own median
convention.kind: d1_over_d5 = first decile / median; d9_over_d5 = ninth decile / median
convention.why_ratios_and_not_dollars: The ratio is the thing that was actually measured, and it is the only form that stays true when the median is re-anchored. A published p10 in local currency belongs to that source's own population, period and exchange rate; our median_wage_full_time_usd is a separately normalised USD figure. Multiplying our median by a measured dispersion ratio puts all three marks on ONE basis, which is what a reader of a single spread is entitled to. The absolute figures that produced each ratio are preserved in _raw for audit, so any ratio can be re-checked against its source.
convention.the_fabrication_ban: A ratio may only be entered when a named source published BOTH the decile and the median it is divided by, from one table and one population. Deriving a decile from quartiles by assuming a distribution shape is forbidden (N9): quartiles relabelled as deciles are a fabricated statistic. A country with no published decile carries no entry here, and its page shows the typical pay alone.

confidence.held: The source published the decile values themselves, for full-time employees, alongside its own median.
confidence.modeled: The source published decile RATIOS (or the population/period differs from our median's basis in a way recorded in _meta.method). Still measured dispersion, never an assumed shape.
confidence.placeholder: Not permitted in this file. A country we cannot source stays absent.

quality_checks.note: Bounds are a unit-error trap, not a plausibility opinion. A d1 above the median or a d9 below it is an ordering bug; a d9/d5 past 4.0 or a d1/d5 under 0.25 is almost certainly a currency, period or population mismatch rather than a real distribution.

_meta.source: Decile ratios of gross earnings, full-time dependent employees, published by the intergovernmental economic research body in its earnings distribution database (dataflow DSD_EARNINGS@DEC_I). Retrieved 2026-08-30 from the public statistical data API. This country's row: D9/D5 2.4, D5/D1 2.5, reference year 2024.
_meta.method: The source publishes dispersion as ratios: D9/D5 (ninth decile over median) and D5/D1 (median over first decile). d9_over_d5 is taken as published; d1_over_d5 is 1 divided by the published D5/D1, recorded to four decimals. Both are then multiplied by this country's own median_wage_full_time_usd in scripts/data/apply_wage_deciles.ts to place the two marks. No distribution shape is assumed anywhere: the ratio is a measured property of that country's own earnings distribution, and the quartile fields in the profile are never read. The dataset's pay-period dimension is coded not-applicable, so the source does not declare whether the underlying earnings are hourly, weekly or annual; for full-time employees the dispersion is close across those bases, but the ratio is transported onto an annual median and that is recorded here rather than hidden.

_meta.method: The source publishes dispersion as ratios: D9/D5 (ninth decile over median) and D5/D1 (median over first decile). d9_over_d5 is taken as published; d1_over_d5 is 1 divided by the published D5/D1, recorded to four decimals. Both are then multiplied by this country's own median_wage_full_time_usd in scripts/data/apply_wage_deciles.ts to place the two marks. No distribution shape is assumed anywhere: the ratio is a measured property of that country's own earnings distribution, and the quartile fields in the profile are never read. The dataset's pay-period dimension is coded not-applicable, so the source does not declare whether the underlying earnings are hourly, weekly or annual; for full-time employees the dispersion is close across those bases, but the ratio is transported onto an annual median and that is recorded here rather than hidden.

_meta.method: Ratios are the published decile divided by the published median from the SAME table and population, then multiplied by this country's own median_wage_full_time_usd. refused.PT: Published 2024 row is D9/D5 2.23, D5/D1 1.07. A D5/D1 of 1.07 puts the bottom ten percent on 93 percent of the median, which breaks a stable 2019-2023 series running 1.31 to 1.40 with a one-year fall of 23.6 percent. Read but not used: a mark drawn on it would almost certainly be wrong. Portugal is instead filled from the European structure of earnings survey, which is the only country in this file not on the harmonised source; see its own entry.
refused.DE_2023: The published 2023 German row is internally inconsistent (D9/D5 3.56 and D5/D1 3.32 multiply to 11.81, against a published D9/D1 of 5.90). The 2024 row is used instead and is consistent.
